title: Single-endpoint normalized reconstruction for exceptional transport
statement: For every field stage and every endpoint scheme in the exceptional transport setup, a normalized reduction/limit reconstruction record exists [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus].

proof.text: Obtain the specified coefficient reduction/total-limit calculus S from lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus. Apply purNormalizedReconstructionOfScheme from lem-pod-unrestricted-normalized-reconstruction to obtain completeness of every normalized limit and invertibility of the actual unit and counit. This version applies to every endpoint scheme without an invertibility hypothesis on l.

Compare IsSfDerivedComplete with IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete by lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison, choosing an auxiliary prime distinct from l. Rewrite cohomological-support containment in [a,b] as IsGE a and IsLE b. The evaluation comparison of S transfers finite constructibility, the same cohomological interval and the same Tor interval. Isomorphism closure of finite constructibility follows from lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated; the explicit Tor interval transfers by composition of representative isomorphisms. Consequently an integral object satisfies finiteTorConstructibleIntegral exactly when it is complete and its reduction satisfies sequenceProperty.

Lift reduction to the finite-Tor integral and normalized uniformly bounded sequence full subcategories. Lift total limit using its completeness and the actual counit isomorphism; transfer the sequence bounds back along that isomorphism. Restrict S.adjunction by Mathlib Adjunction.restrictFullyFaithful with identity comparison squares. Its mapped unit and counit are precisely those of S.adjunction. Reflect their isomorphisms along the full inclusions and apply Adjunction.toEquivalence. Restrict each evaluation using the finite-constructibility component of sequenceProperty. The functor equalities are definitional and the two HEq equations follow from the mapped unit/counit equalities. These constructions give every field of Reconstruction.
